newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDIC settles dispute with Rose Law Firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDIC settles dispute with Rose Law Firm.

text.p: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. said Wednesday it had settled a billing dispute with the Rose Law Firm, where first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton once worked.

In a statement, the FDIC said the firm had agreed to pay $210,911 to settle all outstanding billing disputes arising from the firm's representation of both the FDIC and the Resolution Trust Corp. between 1987 and 1993.
The repayments followed a review by the legal divisions of the two agencies, which confirmed overpayments to the Little Rock, Ark., firm, the statement said.
The Rose Law Firm has already made partial reimbursements of $41,314.37 to the agencies.
The FDIC statement did not give details of the work carried out by the firm for the two agencies.
The period of time covered by the settlement postdates work done by Mrs. Clinton in the mid-1980s for the Madison Guaranty savings and loan, which was also the subject of an FDIC investigation.

As a result of that investigation, the FDIC's inspector general said last September that there was evidence suggesting Mrs. Clinton and law firm partner Webster Hubble helped facilitate a payment of $300,000 in questionable commissions to Hubble's father-in-law.
Hubble resigned in 1994 as the third-ranking official in the U.S. Justice Department and later pleaded guilty to filing false expense accounts and overbilling clients at the Rose Law Firm.
